critical_checks: Repeat misfire if carbon-tracked coil boots are reused.
Plug-well debris can damage threads or keep the new plug from seating.

Fuel trims or misfire counters should be rechecked before delivery.

Weak or carbon-tracked coil boots can mimic plug failure.
Oil in plug wells points to valve cover or tube seal concerns.
inspection_opportunities: Valve cover gasket and plug well seals

repair_snapshot.value: Evidence package before major engine quote

critical_checks: Comeback risk is high if coolant loss is quoted as a head gasket before pressure testing.
Missed radiator cap or external seepage can mimic head gasket symptoms.
A cold-start misfire can return if cylinder evidence is not captured before teardown.
Cooling fan or thermostat faults can recreate the overheat after gasket work.
Document block-test, leak-down, and borescope evidence before major authorization.
known_failure_patterns: Overheating events can create secondary gasket or deck concerns.
External leaks may imitate coolant-loss head gasket symptoms.
Misfire on startup can point to cylinder coolant intrusion.

critical_checks: No-start comeback risk remains if corroded terminal ends are not corrected.
Charging-system faults can return as a dead-battery complaint if output is not checked.
Wrong group size, venting, or chemistry can create fitment and battery-life comebacks.
BMS-equipped vehicles can set warnings or shorten battery life if registration is skipped.
Loose hold-downs can damage the case or cable ends after delivery.
known_failure_patterns: Corroded terminals create repeat no-start complaints.
Weak alternator output can look like battery failure.
Modern battery monitoring systems may need reset.
inspection_opportunities: Parasitic draw if repeated dead battery
